question.problem:
What is the explicit formula for the $n$th term of the arithmetic sequence

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}-3,\,\,{a}_{1}=7,\,\,n\ge 1?
$$
question.worked_solution:
The explicit formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,\,n\ge 1,
$$

so we need to determine the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

We are given that the first term is ${a}_{1}=7,$ and we can use the recursive rule to compute the second term, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} & ={a}_{1}-3 \\  & =7-3 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Using the first and second terms, we can compute the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =4-7 \\  & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute ${a}_{1}=7$ and $d=-3$ into the formula for the $n$th term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =7+(n-1)(-3) \\  & =7-3n+3 \\  & =-3n+10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is

$$
{a}_{n}=-3n+10,\,n\ge 1.
$$
